rounds.proof_sketch: Original returns when blockCol < blockRow. Mutant returns only when 32*blockCol < blockRow-32 (much stricter). Extra blocks that execute have blockRow > blockCol, so loop for(tile=blockRow; tile<=blockCol; tile++) never runs. sum=0.0f. All cells in block satisfy col < row, so 0.0f is written. Output initialized to zeros, so result is identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation allows additional lower-triangular thread blocks to execute instead of returning early. However, these blocks have blockRow > blockCol, causing the inner tile loop (tile = blockRow to blockCol) to have zero iterations. The sum remains 0.0f. When writing output, all cells in these blocks satisfy col < row, triggering the else branch that writes 0.0f. Since the output matrix is pre-initialized with torch::zeros(), writing 0.0f to zero-valued cells produces bitwise identical results. This is a pure performance mutation with no semantic effect.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only affects which blocks execute, not the computed values. Extra blocks compute and write zeros to positions that should be zero. No input values can change this behavior since it depends only on block indices, not tensor values.
rounds.recommendations: This mutation highlights a class of 'performance-only' mutations where early-exit optimizations are relaxed but functional correctness preserved by the kernel's output masking logic. Mutation testing tools should consider marking such mutations as equivalent when: (1) the skipped code path computes neutral values, (2) target memory is pre-initialized to those neutral values, and (3) the mutation only affects which threads execute, not computation logic.
